summary:
AstroCare – Health Monitoring and Decision Support System for Astronauts

AstroCare is an interactive health monitoring and decision-support platform designed to help astronauts understand and manage changes to their health during long-duration space missions.
Our team has developed a web-based prototype that integrates vital signs, personalized comparisons against Earth-based benchmarks, health trends, symptom assessments, body mapping, and guided health reviews. The platform also explores how laboratory biomarkers and environmental conditions can provide additional context regarding an astronaut's health.
AstroCare addresses the challenge of maintaining astronaut health in space, where microgravity, isolation, and communication delays can complicate medical decision-making. Rather than presenting isolated measurements, the platform links health indicators to individual benchmarks, symptoms, and evidence-based assessments, aiming to support informed decision-making and communication with medical teams.
Our solution offers significant value, as future deep-space missions will require health support tools that are more accessible, personalized, and autonomous. Through simulations and illustrative assessment rules, AstroCare demonstrates how scientific research can be translated into practical, simple, and astronaut-centered health monitoring—without, however, replacing professional medical judgment.
details:
AstroCare – Project Details

AstroCare is a web-based platform designed for monitoring astronaut health and supporting decision-making. It was developed to help astronauts track, understand, and respond to physiological changes during long-duration space missions.

How it works

AstroCare consolidates various health indicators into a single interactive platform, including heart rate, blood pressure, body temperature, respiratory rate, oxygen saturation, sleep data, and symptoms reported by the astronauts themselves. By comparing current measurements against personalized baseline parameters, astronauts can understand how their present state differs from their pre-flight health status.

The platform features an interactive body map, health trends analysis, daily self-assessments, and a health review system that provides detailed explanations. Using status categories—indicated by the colors green, yellow, and red—AstroCare helps users identify changes that may require attention. The tool also offers educational guidance and assists in logging health-related events.

Our broader proposal includes the integration of laboratory biomarkers and environmental measurements, aiming to provide an even more comprehensive understanding of astronaut health.

Benefits and Intended Impact

The AstroCare challenge addresses a critical aspect of human space exploration: maintaining astronaut health in situations where access to immediate medical care may be limited by distance, communication delays, or mission conditions.

The app aims to enhance health awareness, support the early identification of concerning changes, encourage confident self-assessment, and facilitate communication between astronauts and medical teams. Our long-term vision is to contribute to the development of more personalized and accessible health support systems for future missions.

Technology and Development

Our team developed AstroCare as an interactive application, accessible online via a dedicated platform. The prototype features a dashboard with visual health indicators, an interactive body map, historical trend charts, and guided assessment workflows.

Innovation and Creativity

The core innovation of AstroCare lies in its integrated, astronaut-centered approach and its ability to provide real-time information. Rather than simply displaying medical measurements, the system links individual health parameters, physiological trends, reported symptoms, and contextual data to provide explainable assessments and suggestions for follow-up actions. The design is grounded in cardiovascular research—specifically the analysis of changes in blood cells—as well as broader studies on human adaptation to spaceflight.

Key Design Considerations

Throughout the development process, our team took into account usability, accessibility, individual physiological differences, the challenges of remote medical support, data interpretation, and astronaut safety.

AstroCare transforms complex health information into an accessible, personalized experience, helping astronauts translate health data into informed actions—without, however, replacing professional medical judgment.
